sources.entry: Atomic Chat - Open-source AI chat client for local and cloud models with MCP support. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/Atomic-Chat)

summary.one_liner: Atomic Chat is an open-source desktop and mobile app for running open-weight LLMs locally, which also exposes an OpenAI-compatible local API and supports cloud providers and MCP servers.
summary.what_it_does: Runs open-weight LLMs locally (models from HuggingFace such as Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, Phi) through three inference engines: a llama.cpp fork with TurboQuant KV cache, upstream llama.cpp, and MLX-VLM for Apple Silicon. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API on port 1337, bound to 127.0.0.1 by default, so existing OpenAI SDK clients can point at it by changing base_url. It also connects to cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, MiniMax, Qwen, Moonshot) with bring-your-own keys, and can connect multiple MCP servers. Extra features include Artifacts previews for HTML/CSS/JS, custom assistants with system prompts, projects, and one-click launch of agents such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cline, OpenCode and Goose from an Integrations tab. The engines are managed by a separate repository, atomic-chat-core.
use_cases: Chat with open-weight LLMs privately on your own computer
Use a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for coding agents or IDE plugins
Compare or mix local models with cloud models in one chat app
Connect MCP tools such as file access or web search to a local model
Run speculative decoding to speed up local inference
Serve local models to other devices on a LAN
notable: OpenAI-compatible local server on port 1337 usable as a drop-in OpenAI SDK replacement
Three inference engines (llama.cpp fork with TurboQuant, upstream llama.cpp, MLX-VLM) behind one API
Speculative decoding options including MTP and DFlash, with platform limits
One-click launch of many coding agents from an Integrations tab
Linux packages via apt, dnf, and AUR, plus AppImage
caveats: Speculative decoding is platform-limited: MTP on macOS and Windows, DFlash on Apple Silicon only, and the two cannot be enabled together
Linux requires glibc 2.35 or newer on x86_64 (2.38+ on arm64) and only GGUF models run there
Building from source needs Node.js 20+, Yarn 4.5.3+, Make, Rust, and on Apple Silicon the MetalToolchain component
